snippets.title: Madhu Guru on models and research
snippets.takeaway: How to build great evals - part 8. The discriminatory property of evals. A hill-climbing eval is useful when it can separate AI systems that are meaningfully different.
snippets.summary: Madhu Guru (realmadhuguru on X) shared 1 recent update. How to build great evals - part 8. The discriminatory property of evals. A hill-climbing eval is useful when it can separate AI systems that are meaningfully different. Imagine you run an eval on five AI systems: A: 94 B: 93 C: 95 D: 94 E: 92 Now suppose you already know A and C are substantially better systems than D and E. The eval is bad cos it doesn’t tell you that. It has low discriminatory power.
